title: add-inference-health-probe-and-sampled-kernel-queue-explorer
author: Priya Nandakumar
description: Adds a lightweight inference health probe and a sampled kernel-queue explorer to improve incident triage and long-tail cost attribution. Motivation: recurring short-lived kernel queue stalls were noisy in SLO pages and made it hard to trace whether slow tails were caused by model-level token spikes, kernel contention, or tenant-induced backpressure. This PR introduces: 1) inference_health_probe: periodic synthetic pings that exercise a small, deterministic token path and emit a health metric (inference_probe_latency_ms) plus an opaque probe_id for trace linking; 2) sampled_kernel_queue_explorer: a new trace sampler that, when a probe or real invocation exceeds a kernel-queue latency threshold, captures a compact kernel-queue snapshot and stores a compacted span with queue_depth, head_kernel_id, and estimated_token_cost_hint; 3) dashboard panels: a compact 'Probe Pulse' timeseries, kernel-queue heatmap (bucketed by queue depth and model shard), and a 'Probe vs Real' latency scatter for quick triage; 4) runbook/playbook: an Observability Surge Playbook page with automated escalation steps and quick links to tenant-level cost and KV cache hit panels. Implementation notes: probe logic is opt-in per deployment via config.inference.probe.enabled (false by default) and probes are low-rate by design (0.1 rps per region) to avoid billing noise; the sampled kernel snapshots are stored in the observability compact store with a capped reservoir to limit cardinality. Backwards compatibility: no changes to public API surfaces. Checklist: [x] add probe runtime hooks, [x] add metric and span schema, [x] add dashboard panels, [x] add playbook and runbook links, [x] update docs and config reference, [x] add unit tests and e2e sampler smoke test. Related: ENG-6123 for incident RCA and OBS-47 for dashboard request. Expected rollout: feature gated for 2 weeks, enable for staging then incrementally to prod with guardrail on stored snapshot volume.
